newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - CalEnergy will not pursue NYSEG.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - CalEnergy will not pursue NYSEG.

text.p: CalEnergy chief executive officer David Sokol said the company has washed its hands of New York State Electric & Gas Corp (NYSEG) and will not pursue the utility again.
In a telephone interview with Reuters, Sokol said CalEnergy is selling its holdings in the New York utility following a decision to drop the acquisition effort.
"We don't think the company is worht $24.50 (per share) without a significant management and strategy change so we are in fact selling our shares that we did own," he said.
Sokol did not specify how many shares are currently held, but said CalEnergy had owned 250,000 of NYSEG's 69 million outstanding shares.

The Nebraska-based independent power producer earlier Friday dropped its monthlong acquisition attempt after not generating enough support in a tender offer for 9.9. percent of NYSEG stock at $24.50 per share.
Sokol said the company is eager to pursue other transactions, saying he would launch another unsolicited effort if necessary.

"We would always choose a friendly transaction, if possible, over a hostile one, but we would be prepared to pursue a transaction if necessary thorugh an unsolicited offer if that was the only way we could get it to the shareholders," Sokol said.
He declined to comment on the region that CalEnergy finds most appealing, saying that the company frequently is involved in discussions about potential transactions.
"We think there are 20 to 30 different U.S. utilities which would allow us to achieve our goals here in the U.S.," he said, adding it also is pursuing Asia and Europe growth.
Sokol said he got the sense earlier this week that the 9.9 percent tender offer for NYSEG was running into trouble.
"I don't want to make excuses. One thing I believe strongly is that shareholders should always be given the right to make a decision. They've made their decision here and we respect that," he said.
However, he cited market expectations that CalEnergy would raise the $24.50 tender offer, and also accused NYSEG of confusing the process with litigation and appeals to state regulators.
